title: Database systems
blurb: Storage engines, query optimization and transactions inside one database, and how its engine evolved.

main.title: CMU 15-445/645: Intro to Database Systems
main.why: Storage, indexes, query execution and optimization, concurrency control and recovery. In English.

main.title: Architecture of a Database System
main.why: System design choices that textbooks skip, such as process models and parallelism, compared across real systems.

main.title: Are You Sure You Want to Use MMAP in Your Database Management System?
main.why: mmap hands paging to the OS, which breaks transactional safety and stalls threads, so several DBMSs moved off it.

main.title: Evolution of Development Priorities in Key-value Stores Serving Large-scale Applications: The RocksDB Experience
main.why: Eight years of RocksDB, as its target moved from write amplification to space, then to CPU.
An LSM tree in place of InnoDB's B+tree halved storage for Facebook's user database.

main.title: The Part of PostgreSQL We Hate the Most
main.why: Postgres copies the whole row on every update, which brings bloat, extra index writes and a hard-to-tune vacuum.

main.title: Yes, PostgreSQL Has Problems. But We're Sticking With It!
main.why: How to live with those problems: measure bloat, drop unused indexes and tune autovacuum.

main.title: An Overview of Query Optimization in Relational Systems
main.why: Search space, cost estimation and enumeration, starting from System R's dynamic programming and interesting orders.

main.title: How Good Are Query Optimizers, Really?
main.why: Cardinality estimates are routinely far off, and they matter more than the cost model.

main.title: A Critique of ANSI SQL Isolation Levels
main.why: The SQL standard's isolation levels are ambiguous, and snapshot isolation still allows write skew.

main.title: Serializable Isolation for Snapshot Databases
main.why: Makes snapshot isolation serializable by detecting the read-write conflicts behind write skew. PostgreSQL's SERIALIZABLE uses it.
More concurrent transactions made each one slower until throughput fell, and a smaller pool fixed it.
How to change a live table's schema without blocking writes or stalling replicas.
Moving 1,200 MySQL hosts to 8.0 over a year: replicas first, with replication back to 5.7 as the way out.
Postgres spends a process on every connection, so Figma built a pooler that rate-limits connections and sheds load.
Detecting a dead primary, promoting a replica and pointing clients at it in 10 to 13 seconds.
Splitting one Postgres into 480 logical shards by workspace, moved over with double writes and dark reads.

main.title: C-Store: A Column-oriented DBMS
main.why: Stores data by column, so an analytical query reads only the columns it needs.

main.title: MonetDB/X100: Hyper-Pipelining Query Execution
main.why: Operators handle a vector of values per call instead of one row, keeping modern CPUs busy.

main.title: DuckDB: an Embeddable Analytical Database
main.why: SQLite's row engine on B-trees is slow at analytics, so DuckDB runs vectorized columnar queries inside the host process instead.

main.title: What Goes Around Comes Around... And Around...
main.why: Twenty years of attempts to replace SQL, and how SQL absorbed their best ideas instead.
